t: What your users actually see These are real captures from a shipping app. Nothing in them is a browser: no address bar, no page chrome, no zoom. h: Why it is built this way
t: Why it is built this way Forms in the Optimum platform are configuration, not code: a tenant adds a field, reorders a step or publishes a whole new application type, and it must be live for customers the same day. Shipping that through an app-store release cycle is not workable. So the SDK splits the problem in three, and each piece does

A native shell Your app owns presentation, the session and the back stack. The SDK gives you a view (React Native, Android), a view controller (iOS) or a modal sheet (Expo) — plus the things a web view cannot do for itself: loading and error interstitials, hardware-back handling, an unsaved-changes guard, authenticated downloads and file

A web form engine The Client Portal renders the form from the tenant's DMS catalogue and submits it to the Optimum Core API. Add a field in the back office and it appears in your app on the next open, with no release. The portal is themed server-side from the branch, so the form already looks like the tenant it belongs to.

One bridge Between them sits Amthal Bridge Protocol v1 — a small, versioned, JSON message contract. Every host implements exactly the same messages, so behaviour is identical across the four runtimes except where the capability matrix below says otherwise. Credentials travel over that bridge, never in a URL.

t: The consequences worth knowing up front The SDK never closes itself on submit. When a submission succeeds you get onSubmitted / formSubmitted with the product id and the application number; what happens next — a confirmation screen, a pop, a second form — is your decision. h: What happens when a form opens
t: What happens when a form opens Worth reading once: almost every support question is really a question about which of these five steps did not complete.

The SDK fetches the manifest GET {baseUrl}/embed/manifest.json — always relative to the full base URL, never to the bare origin. It carries portalVersion , bridgeProtocolVersion and an optional minSdkVersion . Failure here is manifestFailed ; a version mismatch is versionIncompatible .

h: The web view loads the embed route
t: The web view loads the embed route Your request is turned into a path under /embed — for a new application, /embed/form/{type}/{productID} . The SDK's loading interstitial is on screen throughout.

h: The portal says hello, the host replies init
t: The portal says hello , the host replies init init is where the credentials, locale, theme and font scale cross — over the bridge, never in the URL. If no hello arrives within 15 seconds of the page loading, you get bridgeTimeout .

The portal says ready Angular has booted, the credentials have been applied and the first embed route has resolved. This is the moment the SDK hides its skeleton and your onReady fires — exactly once per page load.

h: The user submits — and you decide what happens next
t: The user submits — and you decide what happens next formSubmitted carries productID and, where the portal returns one, applicationNo , batchID and headerID . The SDK does not dismiss itself. If the session expired mid-form instead, you get authExpired , the form pauses, and it resumes the moment you hand back a fresh token. The messages,

6 — Obtain a token Log in with your own call against the same backend the portal uses, and keep the token. The SDK only ever receives it over the bridge.

h: Threat model and the trust boundary
t: Threat model and the trust boundary Three parties share one screen: your application, the Amthal Client Portal running in an embedded WebView, and the network between them. The SDK exists to make the boundary between the first two explicit and narrow. Who trusts what, and where that trust is enforced Party Trusts Does not trust Your app (

The boundary in one sentence The unit of trust is the origin , not the individual script. Once a page is served from the configured portal origin inside the embed subtree, the SDK treats everything running on it as the portal. That is the correct boundary for a WebView, and it is also the limit of what the SDK can enforce — see what this

h: How the bearer token travels, and where it never appears
t: How the bearer token travels, and where it never appears Your app obtains the token with its own login flow; the SDK never mints, refreshes or stores one. It carries it across the boundary in exactly two message types and nowhere else. The credential's complete itinerary Where Present? Detail Bridge init payload Yes Sent as the reply to t

The download header check A downloadRequest message carries both a URL and a header map, and the portal chooses both. If the SDK attached those headers to whatever URL it was given, a compromised or buggy portal page could hand an Authorization header to a third-party host. Both native handlers make the same check before attaching anythin

In-memory handling, and accidental printing The token lives in memory for the life of the session — in BridgeController.currentAuth on iOS, in the view's session state on Android, in a ref on React Native. It is never written to disk by the SDK. Android's PortalAuth overrides toString() to redact all three fields, so a stray log line or c

Main-frame navigation confinement The single most important runtime control. A main-frame navigation is allowed if and only if both conditions hold: its origin is on the allowlist — the baseUrl host plus anything in allowedOrigins — over https (or http for a loopback host, or under an honoured development hatch); and its path is inside th

Sub-frames are deliberately exempt Only the main frame is confined. A legitimate page loads third-party sub-frames — reCAPTCHA, payment widgets, embedded maps — and cancelling one of those does not protect anybody: it externalises a fragment of a page, so the user lands in Safari on google.com/recaptcha/api2/anchor and the form is left be

h: Origin checking on every message and every evaluation
t: Origin checking on every message and every evaluation Confinement stops the main frame moving. h: What destroy() clears — and what it cannot guarantee
t: What destroy() clears — and what it cannot guarantee Teardown is a best-effort protocol exchange, not a transaction. Saying so precisely matters more here than anywhere else on this page, because "the session is cleared" is the kind of sentence a reviewer is entitled to test.
The sequence
Native sends destroy On unmount, on view destruction, or when the host dismisses the sheet. The message goes through the same outbound origin check as any other.

h: The web side clears its persisted auth
t: The web side clears its persisted auth The portal drops its stored user object and branch id ( USER_KEY , BRANCH_ID ) on receipt, regardless of whether its acknowledgement ever gets back .

h: Native waits one second, then releases
t: Native waits one second, then releases A grace window for the ack, then the message handler or JavaScript interface is removed, loading is stopped, pending round-trips resolve to their defaults, and the WebView is released.

Android additionally clears WebView storage WebStorage.deleteAllData() and CookieManager.removeAllCookies() , each wrapped in its own try/catch. h: Pre-ship checklist you can actually run
t: Pre-ship checklist you can actually run Nine checks against a release candidate. Each one either passes or produces a specific thing to go and fix; none of them requires the SDK's source.

h: The base URL carries the deploy path
t: The base URL carries the deploy path Against the production portal, not only staging: It must return JSON with "bridgeProtocolVersion": 1 . HTML means the SPA catch-all answered and the prefix is wrong — which also breaks navigation confinement, because the boundary is computed from that same path.

h: No cleartext hatch in the release configuration
t: No cleartext hatch in the release configuration All three should be empty for the release variant. The flag is inert at runtime in a release build on every platform — but it is still a review finding, and the platform exceptions beside it are not inert at all.

h: enableLogging comes from a debug constant
t: enableLogging comes from a debug constant Expect BuildConfig.DEBUG , __DEV__ or your own equivalent — never a literal true . This matters most on Android, where the flag is honoured in a release build.

h: The token appears in no URL
t: The token appears in no URL Run the app through an intercepting proxy with its CA trusted on a test device, open a form, submit it. The token should appear only in Authorization headers on requests to the portal's own API — never in a request line, query string or fragment, and not at all on GET /embed/manifest.json , which is unauthentic

Confinement holds From inside a form, trigger a link to a URL outside the embed subtree — a different host, or the same host at a path such as /portal/login . The main frame must not move: your onOpenExternal / delegate must fire, or the URL must open outside the WebView. Repeat with a target=_blank link.

Logout really ends the session Sign in, open a form, leave the screen, log out of your app, then reopen the form. It must come back anonymous. If it resumes signed in, either destroy never reached the web layer or your own token was not discarded — both are your integration, not the SDK.

h: Inspect what was left on disk
t: Inspect what was left on disk Download an attachment from a form, then list the app container: cacheDir/amthal-portal/ on Android, tmp/AmthalPortalDownloads/ on iOS. Those files persist after teardown by design. If your policy forbids that, clear them yourself when the session ends.

h: Token storage is Keychain or Keystore
t: Token storage is Keychain or Keystore Confirm in your own code, not the SDK's — this is the single most common real finding in an integration review, and the SDK cannot help you with it.

h: minPortalVersion is set, and its error is handled
t: minPortalVersion is set, and its error is handled Set it to the oldest portal build you have tested. Present versionIncompatible as "please update the app", not as a retry — it is the one error the SDK never auto-retries, because retrying cannot change the answer.

Anything else is cancelled and routed through the openExternal path instead — so an in-portal link to a marketing site opens in the system browser rather than replacing your embedded form.
